text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Wolves at Selhurst Park.

The hosts endured a disappointing season last time out, needing the return of former manager Roy Hodgson to stave off relegation, but they have had a solid start to this one, taking a win, a draw and a defeat from their opening three games to leave them 12th.
A win here could move them as high as fifth in the early stages of this Premier League campaign.

A turbulent pre-season for the visitors saw Julen Lopetegui leave as head coach three days before the campaign got underway, but his replacement Gary O'Neil has stepped in and somewhat steadied the ship, albeit overseeing two defeats from his opening three matches.
A win away at Everton last time out has left fans optimistic that O'Neil can preserve their team's top-flight status after the former West Ham midfielder kept Bournemouth up last season.
Hodgson names an unchanged starting XI from his team's last Premier League outing, a 1-1 draw away at Brentford last weekend.

Despite scoring a 22-minute hat-trick to help the Eagles come from behind against Plymouth Argyle in the EFL Cup in midweek, Mateta remains on the bench as Edouard, who also netted in that game, starts up front.
O'Neil makes two changes from the win at Goodison Park as Ait-Nouri is preferred to Bueno at left-back while Sarabia comes in for Hwang on the wing.
Kalajdzic, who came off the bench to score the dramatic late winner against the Toffees, is again named as a substitute.
New signing Gonzalez could come on for his debut.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch ahead of this big Premier League contest!
The visitors kick us off and we are underway!

Palace have won their last three Premier League home games against Wolves – in their top-flight history they have only won four in a row against Stoke (1969-1973), Southampton (1980-1991) and Wimbledon (1989-1992).
Wolves win the ball high up the pitch and Cunha has options to his left and right.
In the end, he underhits a pass to his right for Neto and Palace scramble clear.
The visitors have enjoyed the better of the opening exchanges, but neither side has been able to fashion a real chance yet.
Neto wins a corner with good work down the left, but a towering header from Andersen clears the resulting set-piece.
The ball does come back into the box, but Silva blasts his shot well over the crossbar.
Guehi receives an early telling-off from the referee after a late challenge on Cunha in midfield as the visitors looked to counter.
Wolves are continuing to threaten.
This time it is Gomes who charges into the Palace box, but his shot is blazed wide of the target.
O'Neil will be very encouraged by his team's start at Selhurst Park.
They have been the side on the front foot, with the Eagles yet to get going.
PENALTY!? Palace players and fans scream for a spot-kick as Eze takes a tumble under a Gomes challenge in the Wolves box as he looked to cut in on his right foot.
VAR does take a look at the incident, but rules that there was not enough contact to award a penalty.
OFF THE LINE!!! Kilman saves a certain goal after an almighty mix-up in the Wolves defence.
Sa underhits a pass to Lemina and Lerma nips in.
He squares it for Ayew, who shoots first time, and the ball looks to be heading in until Kilman makes a goal-saving block.
That is a huge let-off for the visitors!
After a positive start, Wolves very nearly shot themselves in the foot.
Will that provide encouragement for the hosts?
Ayew's deep cross finds Schlupp at the back post, but he cannot get enough power on his effort and Sa easily gathers.
Palace are growing into the game.
Having lost 1-0 to Arsenal in their first home Premier League match this season, Palace are looking to avoid losing their opening two home games in a season for the first time since 2018-19.
Palace have done so five times previously (1994-95, 1997-98, 2004-05, 2017-18, 2018-19), with only West Ham doing so more often in Premier League history (six).
Eze strides towards Sa's goal, getting all the way into the penalty area before an important challenge from Dawson nips the ball away from a corner.
Sa then takes the pressure off his defenders by leaping to claim the lofted set-piece delivery.
Semedo is perhaps unfortunate to receive a yellow card as Schlupp goes down near the corner flag under the full-back's challenge.
Schlupp's floated cross is met by Edouard in the penalty area, but the striker cannot jump high enough to avoid his header soaring high over the crossbar.
Ait-Nouri and Ayew clash after the Wolves man fouls the Palace forward, with the former receiving a booking for his part in the scuffle.
Wolves are left furious as the referee ignores their protests after Neto goes down under Eze's challenge.
Palace fail to fully clear a Wolves free-kick, but Silva's eventual shot from just outside the box balloons over the target.
Since making his Premier League debut, no goalkeeper has made more saves from shots taken inside the box than Sa with 168.
Neto smashes a shot towards Johnstone's goal, but Andersen makes an important block to prevent his goalkeeper from being troubled.
Semedo drags a long-range effort off target as Wolves enjoy a little spell of pressure.
They are still yet to have a shot on target, however.
Edouard requires some treatment after being caught by a stray arm in a coming-together with Dawson.
After a lengthy pause for Edouard to receive treatment, play has now resumed with the Palace striker back on the pitch.
Having only just returned to the field of play, Edouard sees a tame shot easily saved by Sa from a tight angle.
Neto shows some tricky footwork to cut in past Ward and make space for a shot on his right boot.
His effort is decent, but Johnstone is able to tip over for a corner.

Cunha looks as if he will nod Neto's cross from the left towards goal, but there is no shout for Dawson in front of him to leave it, and the former West Ham man gets to it first, skimming a header away from danger, much to Cunha's frustration.
There will be three minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Wolves work the ball really nicely down the left with a clever flick looking to have set Neto up to fire at goal.
The away fans implore him to pull the trigger, but he tries one pass too many and Palace get bodies in the way to clear.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 WOLVES
The game is goalless at the break after an opening 45 minutes of few chances at Selhurst Park.
The hosts came closest with Wolves nearly the architects of their own downfall, as Sa woefully underhit a pass to Lemina.
Lerma stole in before squaring for Ayew, who looked set to fire Palace in front, only for Kilman to get back and make a heroic block to save a certain goal.
Neto looked threatening for the visitors, who shaded the first half without really troubling Johnstone between the hosts' sticks.

O'Neil will be the happier of the two managers at the interval, though he will be keen to figure out how to turn his team's possession advantage into more clear-cut chances, having only registered one shot on target to Palace's three despite having 59.7 per cent of the ball.
Will the Wolves boss look to Kalajdzic again off the bench after his heroics at Goodison Park?
The hosts get us back underway for the second period.
Neither of these sides has scored a first-half goal this season, with this the fourth game of the campaign for both teams.
Wolves have started the second half well, much like they did in the opening 45 minutes.
Can they find a way through this Palace defence?
Ward receives a yellow card for a very late challenge on Neto near the touchline.
Wolves (74) and Palace (70) rank first and second for most Premier League games that were goalless at half-time since the start of the 2018-19 season.
Gomes goes in the book for cynically dragging back Eze after the Palace forward dispossessed him in midfield.
GOAL!!! PALACE TAKE THE LEAD!!! Edouard scores for the second straight game in all competitions, nipping in front of Kilman to get on the end of Mitchell's cross from the left.
He meets the delivery, poking past Sa to put the hosts 1-0 up!
Mitchell's cross was sublime to allow Edouard to fire home.
For all of their good work in this match, Wolves find themselves a goal down and with work to do if they are to avoid a third league defeat of the season.
O'Neil makes his first substitution of the contest, introducing Hwang for Sarabia.
Edouard has scored three goals in his last six Premier League games for Palace, one more than he had in his previous 25.
All three of Edouard's goals this season (all competitions) have come in the second half of matches, with all three goals being scored within the first 15 minutes of the second half.
GOAL!!! WOLVES ARE LEVEL!!! It is the substitute Hwang who gets the equaliser.
He meets Neto's free-kick delivery from the left, with the ball appearing to come off his shoulder rather than his head.
He will not care a jot, though, as the ball flies past Johnstone and into the back of the net to make it 1-1.
Game on!
Neto has impressed in this match, and it was his wicked set-piece delivery that led to Hwang's leveller.
Can Wolves kick on and find a winner now? Their large contingent of travelling supporters will certainly be hoping so.
All three of Wolves' Premier League goals this season have been scored by substitutes (Hwang with two, one for Kalajdzic).
Mateta comes on for Schlupp after scoring a hat-trick in midweek.
Eze's excellent corner delivery is met by Guehi, but his header is straight at Sa, who easily saves.
BIG SAVE! Ait-Nouri badly misjudges an aerial ball and Ayew nicks the ball off him.
The Palace man fires at goal, but Sa is able to get down to his left and tip wide.
Silva makes way for Traore.
Edouard receives the ball from Eze before letting fly at goal, but his left-footed effort is always rising and soars over the bar.
WHAT A STOP! Eze lines up a free-kick, and his powerful effort looks to be flying into the top right corner.
However, Sa leaps to his left and makes an acrobatic save to tip it wide.
GOAL!!! EZE RESTORES PALACE'S LEAD!!! Ward lofts a delivery into the Wolves box, and Mateta is able to divert the ball into Eze's path off his back.
The former Queens Park Rangers man latches onto it, before poking past Sa to put the hosts 2-1 up!
Mateta's unorthodox assist set Eze up to stab home.
Having equalised once already, can Wolves get back to level pegging again to avoid defeat?
Last weekend's hero Kalajdzic is on in place of Gomes as O'Neil looks to haul his side back into the game.
Bueno also enters the fray, with Ait-Nouri making way.
GOAL!!! EDOUARD MAKES IT 3-1!!! It is a brilliant team goal, as Edouard plays the ball to Mateta outside the box.
The substitute's clever flick then gives possession back to Edouard, who finishes into the bottom left corner to surely put the game beyond Wolves' reach.

events.action: finishes into the bottom left corner

text: Mateta gets his second assist since coming off the bench as he tees up Edouard to coolly finish.
It is a long way back for O'Neil's men now if they are to come away from this game with any points.
Neto smashes a curling effort towards goal, and it bounces right in front of Johnstone.
The Palace goalkeeper deals with it well, though, ensuring the ball does not slip out of his grasp with Wolves attackers lurking for any potential fumble.
Having scored two important goals, Edouard makes way for Hughes as Hodgson looks to shore it up.
We are into six minutes of additional time.
Can Wolves get a goal back to set up a nervy finish for the hosts?
Eze looks to add a fourth by trying to pick out the bottom left corner, though Sa gets down well to palm it wide.
The visitors are struggling to get hold of the ball at the moment as the seconds continue to tick away.
Cunha tries to make something happen by charging into the Palace box, but he is crowded out and the hosts clear upfield.
GOAL!!! CUNHA REDUCES THE ARREARS!!! The former Atletico Madrid man gets up well to meet Neto's delivery from the left before heading goalwards.
Johnstone does get a hand to it but cannot stop the ball going in, and it is now 3-2 to Palace.
Can Wolves pull off the dramatic late comeback?
Neto again shows his crossing ability, getting his second assist of the game as he and Cunha give their team a lifeline.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 3-2 WOLVES
The final whistle goes and it is Palace who run out 3-2 winners thanks to Edouard's double and a goal from England international Eze.

Former Celtic striker Edouard put the Eagles ahead when he finished off Mitchell's fine cross in the 56th minute, but Wolves were level shortly after, Hwang coming off the bench to divert Neto's free-kick into the back of the net.

However, it was Palace who would kick on and win the match, with substitute Mateta setting up Eze to put the hosts back in front before also teeing up Edouard for his second to put the game beyond the visitors' reach.
Cunha did pull a goal back in the dying seconds, but it was too little, too late for Wolves who fall to a third defeat of the season.

Palace's great record over Wolves continues having now won five of their six Premier League meetings, with this latest victory enough to move the Eagles up to seventh heading into the international break.
For O'Neil's side, their worrying start leaves them teetering just two points above the bottom three, a position they will be keen to improve on when they return to action.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Crystal Palace's 3-2 victory over Wolves in the Premier League at Selhurst Park.
Goodbye!
